question.prompt: Given that \(x=1\), \(y=-2\) is a solution of the system \(\begin{cases}ax+by=1\\bx-ay=7\end{cases}\), find the value of \(a+b\).

solutions.explanation: Substitution gives \(a-2b=1\) and \(b+2a=7\). From the first equation, \(a=1+2b\). Substitute into the second equation: \(b+2+4b=7\), so \(b=1\) and \(a=3\). Therefore, \(a+b=4\).
solutions.title: Substitute between the coefficient equations

solutions.explanation:
Because \(x=1\) and \(y=-2\) satisfy both equations, substitution gives
\[
a-2b=1,\qquad 2a+b=7.
\]
Multiplying the second equation by \(2\) makes its \(b\)-term cancel the first equation's \(b\)-term when the equations are added:
\[
(a-2b)+2(2a+b)=1+2\cdot7,
\qquad 5a=15.
\]
Thus \(a=3\). The first equation then becomes \(3-2b=1\), so \(b=1\). Therefore, \(a+b=4\).
solutions.title: Eliminate b by addition
